result.title: Calibrate in Context: Efficient Data-Free Quantization from Small Synthetic Pools
result.comment: 21 pages, 5 main figures. Supplementary material included
result.summary: We enable accurate low-bit recovery from small synthetic pools by improving both image synthesis and student preparation. A grid with lower local response error can incur greater error in the student's block context. Functional Grid Calibration (FGC) selects activation scales and integer offsets against full-precision responses constructed from the student's current block input. With weights fixed during calibration, FGC evaluates candidates only at their consuming operators, bringing block context to calibration at nearly local-scoring cost. For DeiT and ViT, progressive inversion updates the same images through increasingly deep teacher prefixes. With 1,000 images, the complete pipeline exceeds MimiQ's reported accuracy in all 18 W4A4/W5A5 settings across nine backbones. With 256 images, DeiT-S and ViT-S reach 68.20% and 66.90% ImageNet top-1 accuracy at W4A4 in 26-27 minutes on one RTX 5090. The pipeline outperforms strengthened 1K-image MimiQ by 13.03 and 24.36 percentage points at lower preparation cost and the same recovery-update count. The same low-budget checkpoints retain their advantage on ImageNetV2.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究 ViT 的小样本合成池无数据量化：用学生网络当前 block 输入的完整精度响应做 Functional Grid Calibration 选择激活尺度与整数偏移，并用渐进反演加深教师前缀来更新同一批合成图像，在 W4A4/W5A5 上以 256–1000 张图取得较好恢复精度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以 block 上下文响应误差而非局部误差来挑选量化参数，可能为低比特压缩下保持 latent 视觉状态的功能保真提供可核查的校准与误差度量线索，但论文任务并非多模态推理，迁移价值需读原文判断。
